question.prompt: Name a track released in connection with the Drake–Kendrick Lamar feud during its March–May 2024 escalation.

answers.evidence: Kendrick Lamar released this diss track on May 4, 2024.
Lamar's appearance on Future and Metro Boomin's March 22 release sparked the feud's 2024 escalation.
Lamar released this diss track on April 30 in response to Drake.
Drake released this track on May 3 as the feud escalated.
Lamar released this response twenty minutes after Drake's “Family Matters.”
Drake's response to “Like That” leaked on April 13 and was officially released on April 19.
Drake released this response on May 5, denying Lamar's allegations.
Lamar posted this diss track on Instagram on May 3.
Drake released this Instagram-exclusive track on April 19 to goad Lamar into responding.
J. Cole released this response to Lamar on April 5 before apologizing and removing it.
Rick Ross released this diss track in response to Drake's “Push Ups.”
Metro Boomin released this instrumental on May 5 in response to an insult on “Push Ups.”
Future and Metro Boomin released an April 21 remix featuring ¥$, on which West attacked Drake and Cole.
Drake released a parody remix of this track on Instagram to promote “Family Matters”; only that remix counts here.
Drake reused the “BBL Drizzy” instrumental on this Sexyy Red song on May 24.

question.explanation: The 2024 escalation involved more than Drake and Kendrick Lamar: J. Cole, Rick Ross, Metro Boomin and others contributed responses, remixes and instrumentals. Instagram-only releases count, as do the feud-related remixes of “Like That” and “Buried Alive Interlude.”
question.criteria: Accept tracks explicitly identified in the document's March–May 2024 account as feud-related diss tracks, responses, remixes, instrumentals, or songs reusing a feud instrumental. Earlier original versions do not count.

provenance.brief: Name a song released during the Drake and Kendrick Lamar feud.

quotes.Not Like Us: Less than a day later, on May 4, Lamar released "Not Like Us", produced by DJ Mustard.
quotes.Like That: On March 22, 2024, Lamar made a surprise guest appearance on Future and Metro Boomin's song "Like That", from their album We Don't Trust You.
quotes.Euphoria: On April 30, Lamar released the diss track "Euphoria".
quotes.Family Matters: On May 3, the feud escalated with Drake's "Family Matters",
quotes.Meet the Grahams: 20 minutes after the release of "Family Matters", Lamar released "Meet the Grahams", produced by the Alchemist.
quotes.Push Ups: On April 13, "Push Ups", Drake's response to "Like That", leaked online.
quotes.The Heart Part 6: On May 5, Drake released "The Heart Part 6".
quotes.6:16 in LA: On May 3, Lamar posted an Instagram Reel containing the diss track "6:16 in LA", similar to how Drake released "Taylor Made Freestyle".
quotes.Taylor Made Freestyle: On April 19, Drake officially released "Push Ups", alongside the Instagram exclusive "Taylor Made Freestyle",
quotes.7 Minute Drill: On April 5, through his mixtape Might Delete Later, Cole released the response song "7 Minute Drill";
quotes.Champagne Moments: Ross responded that day with the diss track "Champagne Moments".
quotes.BBL Drizzy: on May 5, Metro Boomin released "BBL Drizzy", an instrumental that samples an AI-generated R&B parody song referencing a rumor that Drake received a Brazilian butt lift (BBL).
quotes.Like That (remix): on April 21, they followed it with a remix of "Like That" featuring ¥$ (West and Ty Dolla Sign) in which West attacks Drake and Cole.
quotes.Buried Alive Interlude: To promote "Family Matters", Drake released a parody remix of "Buried Alive Interlude", in which he mocks Lamar's rapping abilities and suggests he is basing his claims on social media rumors, via Instagram.
quotes.U My Everything: On May 24, Drake rapped over the "BBL Drizzy" instrumental for his guest appearance on Sexyy Red's song "U My Everything", which Variety described as him trolling Metro Boomin.
